rationale: C10 plausibly supplied a concrete and material drafting template. It addresses the identical task of modifying NAFTA rules of origin in general note 12 to the HTS, uses the same statutory account of section 202 and section 202(q), recalls the same 1993 implementation proclamation, and follows the same operative sequence: Annex-based modification, supersession of inconsistent prior directives, and effective dates for entered or warehoused goods. The child substantially condenses and adapts this machinery for new Canadian and Mexican effective dates. C02 is also a strong earlier analogue for the same rules-of-origin machinery, while C20 closely parallels the child's distinctive delegation to USTR of a later effective date but concerns GSP rather than NAFTA rules of origin.

shared_material.child_excerpt: [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] of December 15, 1993, implemented the North American Free Trade Agreement ... and ... incorporated in the Harmonized Tariff Schedule ... the tariff modifications and rules of origin necessary or appropriate to carry out the NAFTA.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] of December 15, 1993, implemented the North American Free Trade Agreement ... and ... incorporated in the HTS the tariff modifications and rules of origin necessary or appropriate to carry out the NAFTA.
shared_material.explanation: Nearly identical recital establishing the prior implementation and incorporation of NAFTA origin rules into the HTS.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Section 202 ... provides rules for determining whether goods imported into the United States originate in the territory of a NAFTA party ... Section 202(q) ... authorizes the President to proclaim ... the rules of origin ... and to proclaim modifications to such previously proclaimed rules of origin.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Section 202 ... provides rules for determining whether goods imported into the United States originate in the territory of a NAFTA party ... Section 202(q) ... authorizes the President to proclaim the rules of origin set out in the NAFTA and any subordinate tariff categories necessary to carry out the NAFTA Implementation Act.
shared_material.explanation: The child reuses C10's specific statutory recital and adapts the final authorization language to emphasize modification of previously proclaimed origin rules.

shared_material.child_excerpt: In order to modify the rules of origin under the NAFTA, general note 12 to the HTS is modified as provided in the Annex to this proclamation.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: In order to modify the rules of origin under the NAFTA ... general note 12 to the HTS is further modified as provided in Annex II to this proclamation.
shared_material.explanation: This is the same operative legal mechanism and substantially the same language, with the child simplifying the explanation and annex designation.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Any provisions of previous proclamations and Executive Orders that are inconsistent with the actions taken in this proclamation are superseded to the extent of such inconsistency.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Any provisions of previous proclamations and Executive Orders that are inconsistent with the actions taken in this proclamation are superseded to the extent of such inconsistency.
shared_material.explanation: Verbatim supersession clause reinforces the shared operative sequence, although it is not independently decisive.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The modifications made by the Annex ... shall be effective with respect to goods ... entered, or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption, on or after January 1, 2003 ... [or] a date to be announced in the Federal Register by the USTR.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The modifications and technical rectifications ... made by Annexes I and II ... shall be effective with respect to goods entered, or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption, on or after the later of (i) January 1, 2002, or (ii) the 15th day after ... publication ... in the Federal Register.
shared_material.explanation: Both conclude with the same entry-based effective-date machinery; the child adapts it into separate Canadian and USTR-announced Mexican dates.
